new_scholarship.name: International Brock Scholars Award
new_scholarship.duration: Renewable. A student pursuing a four-year honours degree is eligible for a total of three renewals after the first-year award, giving a maximum of four years of funding; a student in a three-year pass degree is eligible for two renewals.
new_scholarship.deadline: No separate scholarship application and therefore no separate scholarship deadline. The award is automatic: the International Brock Scholars Award is 'offered at the time of admission'. The only published deadline condition is that the student must 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office' in order to confirm the award. The International Ambassador Award is the one award on the page that does require its own application, and it is marked '2026 Application Closed'.
new_scholarship.application_period: There is no scholarship application window for the International Brock Scholars Award. It is assessed automatically from the admission average at the point an offer of admission is made, for each incoming international student entering a first undergraduate programme in the Fall term. Brock publishes the amount tiers on its 2026-2027 international students page, so the currently published figures are the 2026 entry amounts.
new_scholarship.application_method: Automatic on admission. No application is required. Brock states: 'Brock Scholars awards are open to incoming students from anywhere in the world. To qualify, you must be entering your first undergraduate program in the Fall term (no previous post-secondary experience). No application is required.' The award is 'offered at the time of admission and may increase or decrease if your final average changes.' This is the opposite of the separate-application awards on the same pages, which are made by committee selection and require a dedicated application form, and of the OneApp, which is the route for hundreds of other Brock awards and bursaries.
new_scholarship.description: The International Brock Scholars Award is Brock University's largest award and its main automatic entrance award for students from outside Canada. Brock states it is 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world' who is entering their first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and that 'No application is required'. The award is an academic distinction based on final admission average and carries a renewable financial component that is applied directly against tuition fees. Published 2026 first-year amounts for international students range from CAD $7,000 to CAD $32,000 depending on the final admission average, with renewal amounts of CAD $4,000 to CAD $20,000. Award amounts are described by the University as 'subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change'.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International applicants from any country who will enter their first undergraduate degree at Brock University in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and who reach a final admission average of at least 80 per cent. The maximum award requires a final admission average of 95 per cent or above. Applicants from the USA are not eligible for the international tiers; they qualify for the Domestic Brock Scholars Entrance Award instead. Students already holding a tuition waiver do not receive the tuition-offset component.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: The applicant must be entering their first undergraduate programme at Brock University in the Fall term and must have no previous post-secondary experience. There is no citizenship or nationality restriction: the award is open to incoming students 'from anywhere in the world'. The award is set by final admission average, with a published minimum of 80 per cent for international students; below 80 per cent the applicant 'will no longer be eligible for a Brock Scholars award'. The admission average is calculated on the prerequisites for the offered programme of study, calculated to the nearest tenth of a percent and not rounded. Non-Ontario curricula are assessed by the Admissions Office and the criteria vary by curriculum. Students from the United States qualify only for the Domestic Brock Scholars Entrance Award amounts. Full-time study is required, with a minimum of 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: There is no competition or committee selection for this award. Brock describes it as 'an academic distinction based on admission average grade', so selection is purely by final admission average against the published tiers. The award is offered at the time of admission and 'may increase or decrease if your final average changes'. Initial offers are made on secondary school grades available at the time of admission, and the offers are revised when final grades are submitted. The admission average is calculated using the prerequisites for the offered programme of study, to the nearest tenth of a percent, and Brock states 'We do not round averages up or down'. Renewal is separate and is assessed after each 5.0 credit milestone against the student's best 5.0 full credits, requiring a minimum 80 per cent average in each milestone, assessed at 5.0, 10.0 and 15.0 cumulative credits. No published selection weighting percentages beyond the average bands.
new_scholarship.notes: Award selection: the assigned slot named 'Brock University International Scholarships', which is a family of awards rather than one award. Brock publishes several bachelor's-level awards open to incoming international students on one host. The International Brock Scholars Award was chosen because it is by far the best documented and the only one that is automatic rather than committee-selected: it is described by Brock as 'Our largest award', it publishes a full four-tier amount table with separate first-year and renewal figures, explicit admission-average criteria, renewal rules, course-load conditions and confirmation requirements. Other incoming-international awards on the same page were not recorded as separate records, so there is no duplicate-award conflict: the Brock Future Leaders Scholarship (CAD $10,000, 10 awards, committee selection, separate application), the International Curriculum awards (CAD $3,000, first 20 accepted international fee-paying students holding an international curriculum), the International Ambassador Award (variable, equal to domestic tuition rates, committee selection, and whose 2026 application is marked closed), the Brock Canadian High School Excellence Award (CAD $2,000, first 30 accepted international fee-paying students graduating from a Canadian high school), and the International Transfer Award (CAD $3,000, first 10 accepted international fee-paying transfers). The Caribbean International Scholarship (CAD $4,000) was deliberately NOT recorded as a candidate because Brock restricts it to a named list of Caribbean countries, which the research protocol lists as a hard-excluded region. Tuition coverage: the award is explicitly a partial tuition offset, applied directly to tuition fees, so tuition_coverage is true but fully_funded is false; there is no published living-cost component, and a student already holding a tuition waiver receives the distinction but not the tuition offset. No bond or service obligation is published. The Brock Future Leaders Scholarship application form is hosted on forms.office.com, a third-party form host, so that URL is not cited as an official source. logo_override is null pending a verified official-domain image; the brocku.ca pages lazy-load their logo behind a data: URI SVG placeholder, so the header image URL could not be read from the fetched markup.

programme_detail_official.deadline_note: No exact calendar date is published for this award and none has been invented. Brock publishes no scholarship application deadline because there is no scholarship application: the award is automatic and 'offered at the time of admission'. The only date-bearing instruction in the published terms is the confirmation requirement to 'Reply to your offer of admission by the deadline specified by the Registrar's Office', and Brock does not publish that date on the scholarship pages; it is programme- and term-specific and is published by the Registrar's Office. A related hard date is published for transcripts rather than for the award: Brock states that official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The award is open because it has no application window to close: Brock states the awards are 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world' and that 'No application is required'. At the verification date of 2026-10-03 Brock's published amount tables are the 2026-2027 entry figures, and the page footer carries a 2026 copyright. The one separate-application international award on the same page, the International Ambassador Award, is marked '2026 Application Closed', which confirms that the automatic award itself remains open for current applicants.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Renewable. Three renewals in a four-year honours degree (maximum four years of funding in total) or two renewals in a three-year pass degree.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is applied against tuition, not paid as an unrestricted stipend. Brock states that the award 'currently includes a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees' and that 'Your scholarship will be applied directly to your tuition fees. This will take place before classes begin in September, reducing the amount you owe to the University.' tuition_coverage is therefore true in the sense that the money directly reduces tuition. However the University explicitly calls it a partial offset, the published maximum of CAD $32,000 is a fraction of a full international tuition load, and no tuition-fee waiver, living-cost, residence or travel component is published, so fully_funded is false. Two published limits apply: scholarships 'cannot be used for first instalments or down payments', and 'students already holding a tuition waiver will have the academic distinction noted on their transcript but will not receive the tuition offset funding'.

Applied directly against tuition as a partial offset; renewable for up to three further years. Not full funding, and no living-cost component is published.

programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: This is specifically the international version of the award, with its own amount table published on Brock's 2026 International Students page. Students who become domestic students or gain status to pay domestic tuition rates have the international award 'converted to the Domestic Brock Scholars to align with the change to domestic fees'.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Automatic on admission, not a separate application. The published terms are explicit on both points: 'Brock Scholars awards are open to incoming students from anywhere in the world. To qualify, you must be entering your first undergraduate program in the Fall term (no previous post-secondary experience). No application is required.' And 'A Brock Scholars Award is offered at the time of admission and may increase or decrease if your final average changes.' For contrast, Brock's other incoming-international awards such as the Brock Future Leaders Scholarship and the International Ambassador Award are made by committee selection and do require their own application form, and the OneApp is the separate application route for hundreds of other awards and bursaries.

programme_detail_official.description: The International Brock Scholars Award is Brock University's largest award and its automatic entrance award for students from outside Canada. Brock states that it is 'open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world', requiring only that the student be entering their first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, and that 'No application is required'. The award is an academic distinction based on final admission average and carries a renewable financial component that partially offsets tuition fees and is applied directly against them before classes begin in September. Published 2026 first-year amounts range from CAD $7,000 to CAD $32,000, with renewal amounts from CAD $4,000 to CAD $20,000. Award amounts are subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change.
programme_detail_official.coverage: A renewable tuition offset for incoming international undergraduates, tiered by final admission average: first-year amounts of CAD $32,000, CAD $24,000, CAD $12,500 or CAD $7,000, and renewal amounts of CAD $20,000, CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000. The money is applied directly to tuition fees. It is explicitly a partial offset rather than full tuition, and no living-cost, residence, meal, travel or health component is published for this award.

application_readiness_checklist: Do not look for a scholarship form. This award is automatic: Brock states 'No application is required', so the only thing you submit is an undergraduate admission application as an international fee-paying student

Aim for a final admission average of at least 80 per cent, because below that 'you will no longer be eligible for a Brock Scholars award'; the tiers at 95.0 and above, 90.0-94.9, 85.0-89.9 and 80.0-84.9 are worth very different amounts
Make sure you are entering your first undergraduate programme in the Fall term with no previous post-secondary experience, since both conditions are required to qualify
If you are applying from the United States, check the domestic award instead; Brock states 'U.S.A. applicants will only qualify for Domestic Brock Scholars Award amounts'
If you already hold a Brock tuition waiver, understand that you receive the academic distinction but not the tuition offset funding, because Brock states those two are mutually exclusive

Reply to your offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, since confirming the scholarship requires it alongside the name, programme, year of study and likeness release, and full-time registration
Register a full-time course load of at least 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms, because reducing to part-time pro-rates or withdraws the award
Watch the transcript cut-off. Brock states official transcripts 'will only be accepted until Oct. 31' for scholarship revisions, and summer courses taken after graduation will be used in the revision

If you are a co-op student, complete the Brock Scholars Award Renewal Form so that your renewal is reviewed, and note that work-term additive credit courses used for the co-op certification are excluded from the milestone calculation
If you are in a three-year pass degree, plan for two renewals rather than three; honours degrees of four years get three
If you intend to apply for OSAP, do not list this scholarship under Award Income in the OSAP application, because Brock reports it on your behalf
common_rejection_risks: Hunting for a scholarship application that does not exist and assuming there is a deadline to meet; this award requires no application at all
A final admission average below 80 per cent, which ends eligibility entirely rather than reducing the tier
A final average that lands below the band offered on the provisional offer, because Brock states the award 'may increase or decrease if your final average changes'
Applicants with previous post-secondary experience, who are excluded because the award requires entering a first undergraduate programme
Applying from the USA and expecting the international tiers, which Brock says are unavailable to USA applicants
Missing the Registrar's Office reply deadline for the admission offer, which is the only step that confirms the scholarship
Dropping below a full-time course load, which causes the tuition offset or scholarship to be pro-rated or withdrawn
Falling under 80 per cent in a 5.0 credit milestone and losing the renewal
Expecting the award to pay living costs, housing or travel; it is a tuition-only partial offset
Relying on it to cover a first instalment or down payment, which Brock explicitly excludes
estimated_uncovered_costs: The majority of international tuition fees. Even the top tier of CAD $32,000 in year 1 is only a partial offset and the University describes it as 'a renewable financial component to partially offset tuition fees'
All renewal tuition above CAD $20,000 per year at the top tier, and above CAD $15,000, CAD $8,000 or CAD $4,000 at the lower tiers
Non-instructional and other program-related fees; the award is applied to tuition and no separate fee coverage is published
Residence and meal plan costs, for which no coverage is published on the award page

Health insurance. Brock publishes Universal Health Insurance Plan (UHIP) as mandatory health insurance coverage for all international students, plus a BUSU Health and Dental Plan described as a mandatory fee for all international students, and an International recovery fee of CAD $750 charged by the Province of Ontario to all international students at public colleges and universities
Any tuition instalment or down payment, which the scholarship cannot be used for
Study permit fees, travel to Canada and other arrival costs not named in the published provision
document_audit: Confirm your Brock admission application was submitted as an international fee-paying student, since the international tiers do not apply otherwise
Track the Oct. 31 cut-off for official transcripts so that any scholarship revision based on final grades is processed
Keep your final admission average to one decimal place in mind, because Brock calculates to the nearest tenth of a percent and states 'We do not round averages up or down'

If you took a non-Ontario curriculum, get your Admissions Office assessment of how your final average is computed, because Brock states the criteria 'will vary by curriculum, and will be determined by the Admissions Office'
For co-op students, ensure the Brock Scholars Award Renewal Form is filed, since renewal is otherwise not reviewed

Reply to your offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, agree to the name, programme, year of study and likeness release, and register full time. That is what confirms the scholarship.
Award amounts are subject to annual approval by the Board of Trustees and are subject to change, so the figures published for 2026 entry are not a guarantee for later entry.
Renewal is assessed at 5.0, 10.0 and 15.0 cumulative credits against your best 5.0 full credits, and requires at least 80 per cent in each milestone.

submission_workflow: Apply for admission to a Brock University undergraduate programme as an international fee-paying student
Receive the offer of admission carrying the Brock Scholars Award, calculated from the admission average of the prerequisites for your offered programme
Reply to the offer of admission by the Registrar's Office deadline, agree to the release of your name, programme, year of study and likeness, and register a full-time course load
Submit final official transcripts by Oct. 31 if the award figure needs revising
Study full time, at least 1.50 credits in each of the Fall and Winter terms
At each 5.0 credit milestone, achieve at least 80 per cent to have the award renewed, and file the renewal form if you are a co-op student

research_notes.logo: Logo hunt attempted and unsuccessful, so logo_override is null, which the contract states is an acceptable and honest outcome. What I tried: (1) Read the fetched markup of https://brocku.ca/safa/2026-international-students/, https://brocku.ca/safa/2026-future-students/ and https://brocku.ca/safa/awards-and-bursaries/. In all three the header logo appears only as the alt text 'Brock University logo' pointing at https://brocku.ca/, with the actual image src replaced by a lazy-loading placeholder of the form data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%201800%201100'%3E%3C/svg%3E. That is a zero-content inline SVG used as a lazy-load sentinel, so the real header image URL is not present in the server-rendered markup and cannot be read without executing JavaScript. The same pattern was seen for every other image on those pages, including the decorative illustrations and the two footer CTAs. (2) Because no logo URL was extractable from the official pages, I did not guess candidate paths such as /images/logo.svg or /assets/logo.png, since rule 5 forbids an unprobed URL and PART D forbids inventing a plausible-looking one. I stopped rather than probe blind paths. Not used at any point: any aggregator, CDN mirror, Wikimedia, stock site or social-host asset. Brock is also absent from the taken-logo-host list in EXISTING_AWARDS.md, so a future verified brocku.ca logo would be a new key rather than a duplicate, but nothing was recorded without live verification of real image bytes.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The Brock Scholars Awards section of the official Future Students page states: 'Brock Scholars awards are open to incoming students from anywhere in the world. To qualify, you must be entering your first undergraduate program in the Fall term (no previous post-secondary experience). No application is required.' This is corroborated independently by the official 2026 International Students page: 'Our largest award is the Brock Scholars awards. These awards are automatic and open to every incoming student from anywhere in the world. To qualify, you must be entering your first undergraduate program (no previous post-secondary experience).' Both pages describe a first undergraduate degree programme, and the renewal terms refer to three-year pass degrees and four-year honours degrees, which are bachelor's programmes.
research_notes.award_selection_rationale: The assigned slot named 'Brock University International Scholarships', a family rather than a single award. Brock publishes several bachelor's-level awards open to incoming international students. The International Brock Scholars Award was selected because it is the best documented and the only automatic one: Brock itself calls it 'Our largest award', and it is the only award on the page that publishes a complete four-tier amount table with distinct first-year and renewal figures, explicit admission-average criteria, renewal milestone rules, course-load conditions, confirmation requirements and disbursement mechanics. The committee-selected awards each require a separate application form, are limited in number, and do not publish renewal mechanics. Only one record was written for brocku.ca so there is no duplicate-award conflict on this host; the other international awards are recorded in supplements_or_initiatives as context.
